blocks.text: Two NASA views of the same evidence: the air each test burned in, and the one measured flammability boundary.
Every solid-material test we could place: oxygen before ignition (up) against total pressure (across). 134 tests, one dot each.
BASS-II on the ISS: all 129 tests at 1 atm, the pressure of Earth's air, from 13.6% to 22.2% O2.
SSCE: 35, 50, 70% O2 at 1–2 atm. NASA does not say which O2 went with which pressure, so these are ranges.
Moon bases and rovers: ≥30% O2 at ≤70.33 kPa. Inside, only Saffire VI-2 and Saffire VI-3. Hover the box for what is missing.
Same oxygen per breath: along the dotted line, pO2 equals sea-level air's 21.2 kPa. 30% at 70.33 kPa gives 21.1 kPa.
Spacesuits: 100% O2 at 29.65 kPa. No solid test in our sources burned in that air.
Our sources hold one measured flammability boundary: NASA's fit for PMMA rods in BASS-II. Above the line flames burn; below, they go out.
Too little flow quenches the flame; too much blows it off. Lowest point: 13.61% O2 at a = 10.38 1/s.
Only 7 flight tests can be rebuilt from public PSI files: 3 last stable flows (●) and 4 blowoffs, true value at or left of the marker (◂).
Every BASS-II test ran at 1 atm. Our sources hold no flammability boundary at Moon-base pressure.
Of the solid-material space fire tests in our sources, only 2 burned in Moon-base air (Saffire VI-2 and VI-3), both at one airflow (20 cm/s), none in partial gravity.

NASA's published fit (report sec. 6.1.4.4, p.75): above the line PMMA rods burn, below they go out. Solid over a = 4.75–182.95 1/s (every Olson flow recorded in cm/s), dashed beyond. Computed minimum 13.61% O2 at a = 10.38 1/s.
Only 7 of NASA's ~50 ISS boundary points can be reconstructed from the public PSI files.
Most extinction (quenching-branch) flows are recorded only as fan pot settings (0.27-0.36) below the lowest calibrated pot (0.5).
Drop-tower data are not in PSI.
Our count of plotted ISS symbols (about 27 stable, 16 blowoff, 8 quench); the report states no total.
NASA's own plot, for comparison (image only; points not digitized). BASS-II Summary Report, NASA/TM-20210011385 (Oct 2021), p. 76

The only boundary in our sources (BASS-II eq. 6.1, PMMA rods) was measured in microgravity. At Earth gravity there is none.

Flight video from NASA PSI (BASS-II, PSI-25). The on-screen date is one day ahead of the test date (the FAQ says leap year was not set on board). FUEL, AIR, FAN and RAD are the on-board displays; nothing here is read off the video by software.
O4: flame goes out as the flow is turned down

A 3/8-inch clear PMMA rod burning at its upstream tip. The crew lowered the fan step by step; the flame shrinks and goes out about 21 s into this clip. On-screen AIR is the duct flow display in cm/s; it responds in about 1 min (report p.66).
Air display (duct flow, cm/s), as noted by the crew
Fan display (crew setting: pot or fan voltage ×10), as noted
Steps in the order written; no times are given. Raw notes: Fan "5, 0.7, 0.5, 0.4, 0.36 ext" · Air "5, down to ext".
O4 · Olson · 2014-07-08 · PMMA rod, upstream ignition (stagnation / concurrent) (0.375")
Last stable flow before extinction, Air 5 cm/s (the extinction flow itself is below the fan calibration): a = 19.399 1/s at 13.6% post-burn O2 · Evidence Map
O7: blowoff when the fan is stepped to maximum

The on-screen FAN readout jumps to 122 (fan voltage x10, its maximum). The flame is pushed back and blows off about 15 s into this clip, while the AIR readout is still climbing. That lag is why Panel 2 treats blowoff flows as upper bounds.
